problem: Given that $n\ge 9$ is an integer, simplify $\frac{(n-8)!\,(n+9)!}{(n-9)!\,(n+7)!}.$

feedback.problem: Given that $n\ge -3$ is an integer, simplify $\frac{(n+6)!}{(n+5)\text{ }(n+3)!}=$
feedback.worked_solution:
First, we notice that

$$
(n+6)!=(n+6)(n+5)(n+4)(n+3)!
$$

Then, we can cancel the $(n+5)$ and $(n+3)!$ that occur in both the numerator and the denominator:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{(n+6)!}{(n+5)\text{ }(n+3)!} & =\frac{(n+6)\cdot (n+5)\cdot (n+4)\cdot (n+3)!}{(n+5)\cdot (n+3)!} \\  & =\frac{(n+6)\cdot \cancel{(n+5)}\cdot (n+4)\cdot \cancel{(n+3)!}}{\cancel{(n+5)}\cdot \cancel{(n+3)!}} \\  & =(n+6)\cdot (n+4) \\  & ={n}^{2}+10n+24\end{aligned}
$$
